# macpymessenger

> A typed Python 3.14+ library and command-line tool that sends text through the built-in macOS Messages app with a private-data-safe AppleScript transport.

macpymessenger is local and send-only. It has no runtime dependencies. It does not read chat history, send attachments, resolve contacts, expose a remote gateway, or manage a Messages account. The first send may require Automation permission for the application that launches Python.

The core data flow is `IMessageClient` → immutable `SendRequest` → `MessageTransport`. The default `AppleScriptTransport` invokes fixed argv `('/usr/bin/osascript', '-')` and sends encoded AppleScript through standard input, keeping recipient and message text out of process arguments and temporary files.

## Start here

- [Documentation](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): Product scope, quick start, and documentation map.
- [Installation](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation.html): macOS, Python, Messages, Automation, and correct uv command usage.
- [Command line](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/command-line.html): JSON over standard input, stable output, exit codes, and version-matched Agent Skills.
- [Environment diagnostics](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/environment-diagnostics.html): Side-effect-free doctor command, blocker semantics, manual checks, JSON schema, and exit codes.
- [Send from Python](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/sending-messages.html): Single sends, delays, sequential bulk results, privacy boundary, and error handling.

## Agent entry point

Load the instructions bundled with the installed package before sending:

```bash
macpymessenger skills get core
```

Inside a uv project, use `uv run macpymessenger skills get core`. The installed skill defines the current request shape, result shape, exit codes, permission checks, privacy boundary, and retry rule.

## Guides

- [Templates](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/templates.html): Callable Python 3.14 t-string templates with normal conversion and formatting.
- [Logging](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/logging.html): Application-owned Python logging with generic built-in delivery outcomes.
- [Troubleshooting](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/troubleshooting.html): Automation, account, installation, transport, delay, and template failures.

## API reference

- [API map](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules.html): Supported public surface and scope boundaries.
- [Client API](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/client.html): `IMessageClient` and immutable `BulkSendResult`.
- [Transport API](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/transport.html): `SendRequest`, `MessageTransport`, and `AppleScriptTransport`.
- [Template API](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/templates.html): In-memory template registration and rendering.
- [Exceptions](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/exceptions.html): Reachable failures and `MessageFailureReason`.
- [Diagnostics](https://macpymessenger.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/diagnostics.html): `EnvironmentCheck`, `EnvironmentReport.blocked`, and `CheckStatus`.

## Agent rules

- Run `macpymessenger skills get core` before using the command.
- Run `macpymessenger doctor --json`; do not parse human output.
- Treat `blocked: false` as “no automated blocker found,” not “delivery proven.” Complete every check whose status is `manual`.
- Feed one closed JSON object to `macpymessenger send --json` through standard input. Never infer a recipient, message, or permission to send.
- Do not retry a failed or uncertain send automatically; a retry can duplicate a message.
- Inject a `MessageTransport` in tests. Never invoke Messages or AppleScript during ordinary automated tests.
- Keep real recipients, message bodies, account data, and private paths out of process arguments, environment variables, temporary files, logs, tracebacks, fixtures, examples, issues, and commits.
- Run the exact verification commands in `AGENTS.md` before claiming completion.
